questions.q: In a Conditional Column with multiple clauses, in what order are they tested?
options: Top to bottom, and the first match wins
Bottom to top
All at once, and the last match wins
Randomly each time the query runs
questions.explain: Clauses are evaluated in order from top to bottom. As soon as one clause's condition is true, its output is used and the remaining clauses are skipped.

questions.q: What data type does a newly created Conditional Column have by default?
options: Any — you should set the correct type afterward
Whatever type the first clause's output column has
Text, always
It matches the New Column Name's implied type
questions.explain: New conditional columns come in as the Any data type. You need to explicitly set the correct type afterward, the same way covered in Lesson 13.

questions.q: How does Column From Examples work?
options: You type example output values, and Power Query infers a transformation that produces them
You write M code directly into a text box
It only works on numeric columns
It automatically applies to every column in the table at once
questions.explain: You type what the result should look like for one or more rows, and Power Query infers the underlying transformation, filling in the rest of the rows automatically.

questions.q: After Column From Examples creates a new column, what happens to it?
options: It becomes a real, permanent, editable step in the query, just like any other transformation
It's a temporary preview only, and disappears when you close the file
It can never be edited or removed afterward
It replaces the original column it was built from
questions.explain: The column becomes a genuine Applied Step (like "Inserted Range") — fully inspectable and editable, not a special or temporary kind of column.

questions.q: When is Conditional Column the better choice over Column From Examples?
options: When you already know the exact rule you want to apply (if X, then Y)
When you don't know what result you want at all
Conditional Column is always better in every case
When working with more than 100 rows
questions.explain: Conditional Column is for when you know the exact if/then/else logic already. Column From Examples is better when you know the desired result but aren't sure how to produce it.
